decisions: 0110 SET ITS OWN RELEASE CONDITION AND IT WAS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED. It said the flat column is 'retired in a later migration once per-type prices are entered and the trip backfill is verified'. Both held: every station carries a per-type price, and water_stations_offers_at_least_one_type was ALREADY convalidated - the second item 0110 parked, closed by someone before this, so 0122 does not touch it.

LOSING AN UNUSED NUMBER BEATS INVENTING A BUSINESS FACT. The only datum 0122 destroys is olaya_filling_point.fill_cost = 70.00. Olaya has ZERO trips all time, so it had never priced a fill - no P&L figure and no frozen trips.filling_cost_sar traced to it. Writing it into fill_cost_potable_sar to 'save' it would have asserted that Olaya offers potable, because NULL there MEANS 'not offered' under this schema's central rule. The migration carries a DO-NOT-FIX block and its check B asserts Olaya's potable is still NULL afterwards. Same trap 0110 avoided and the same one that got a seed migration drafted and deleted during the Water Station Cost work.

NO APP COMMIT WAS NEEDED, WHICH MADE 0122 UNLIKE 0119 AND 0121. Every remaining mention of the column was a COMMENT saying it was deprecated, and no TypeScript type declared it - StationPricing names only the per-type pair - so nothing selected it into a typed shape. Verified rather than trusting section 7's 'app code already ignores it'.

THE MONEY PROOF IS A BEFORE/AFTER, NOT AN ARGUMENT. v_filling_cost_monthly was byte-identical across the apply: Jun 210.00 (18 costed / 10 uncosted), Jul 1,285.00 (143/3), Aug 5,185.00 (598/0), trips 817 / 13. Dropping a column no view reads cannot reach the P&L, and the check demonstrates that rather than asserting it.

REGEX TRAP, worth carrying: use fill_cost[^_], never %fill_cost%. The loose pattern also matches fill_cost_potable_sar / fill_cost_non_potable_sar and returns false positives on every dependency check - including the three fill_cost-NAMED constraints on water_stations, which reference ONLY the per-type columns. Read constraint definitions, not their names.

RE-MEASURE A DEFERRED ITEM'S PREMISE BEFORE EXECUTING ON IT. Applied twice now. On 0121 the premise was WRONG (a 'concept-merge' with zero rows to merge). On 0122 it was RIGHT but incomplete - the note implied a constraint still needed validating when it had already been done.

REVIEW PACKS GET A CLOSED HEADER AND A PERMANENT NAME. The body stays unedited because the argument as it was made is the record; the header carries the outcome so a committed pack cannot be read as a live 'NOT APPLIED' claim. .planning/for-review.md is the architect's MAILBOX and is left empty between rounds.
